questions.q: Where in Setup is implicit sharing configured?
options: Setup > Sharing Settings > Sharing Rules
Setup > Digital Experiences > Settings
Nowhere — it is not configured anywhere; it follows automatically from Account-to-child object relationships
Setup > Territory Settings
questions.explain: Unlike sharing rules or teams, implicit sharing has no dedicated configuration screen — it's an automatic consequence of how Account relates to Contacts, Opportunities, and Cases.

questions.q: A user has Edit access to one specific Opportunity through manual sharing. What access, if any, do they implicitly get to that Opportunity's parent Account?
options: Full ownership transfer of the Account
Edit access to the Account, matching the Opportunity's access level
No implicit access at all
Read-only access to the Account, regardless of the Edit level they have on the Opportunity
questions.explain: Parent sharing always caps at Read on the parent Account, no matter what access level the user holds on the child record.

questions.q: What role-level setting determines whether a user's access to an Account implies access down to that Account's Contacts, Opportunities, and Cases?
options: The Account owner's role child access settings (View / View and Edit)
The object's organization-wide default
The Territory Type assigned to the Account
The Apex sharing reason attached to the Account
questions.explain: Child sharing depends on the Account owner's role being configured with child access settings — View or View and Edit — for Opportunities, Contacts, and Cases.

questions.q: Why is implicit sharing a common cause of 'unexplained' access during a visibility audit?
options: Because it is disabled by default in all new orgs and rarely encountered
Because it only ever applies to Apex managed sharing rows
Because implicit sharing always requires Modify All Data to take effect
Because it grants access through Account-child relationships with no row in a sharing rule, team, or manual-share related list to point to
questions.explain: Implicit access flows from object relationships and role child-access settings rather than from any explicit, inspectable grant, so an audit that checks only rules/teams/manual shares will under-report real access.

questions.q: What does enabling faster account sharing recalculation change?
options: It stops storing persistent implicit share rows and evaluates access dynamically instead, with no change to end-user visibility but a change to what SOQL can query
It removes implicit sharing entirely, so parent/child access no longer applies
It converts all implicit shares into Apex managed sharing rows with custom RowCause values
It changes which license types are eligible for implicit sharing
questions.explain: The feature changes the underlying mechanism from stored share rows to dynamic evaluation — visible end-user access is unchanged, but Apex/tests that query the old implicit share rows directly will return nothing.
